prompt.context: Our client, DigiBooks, is a manufacturer and seller of electronic book readers (tablets). DigiBooks also distributes e-books for the tablets through their website. The tablet is only compatible with books sold through the DigiBooks site. DigiBooks is planning the launch of its tablets in a country where no electronic book readers are currently sold. Only 1% of the population has ever used an electronic book reader, though 50% is aware of the concept. The Chief Marketing Officer of DigiBooks has come to you to help determine how DigiBooks should launch and market DigiBook tablets in this new country.
prompt.question: How should DigiBooks launch and market DigiBook tablets in this new country?

clarifying_info.q: What is an electronic book reader?
clarifying_info.a: A software, hardware and network platform that utilizes wireless connectivity to enable users to shop for, download, browse, and read e-books, newspapers, magazines, blogs, and other digital media.

clarifying_info.q: What are the specifications of DigiBooks' tablet?
clarifying_info.a: It uses an e-ink electronic paper display that features 16 shades of grey, allowing for a 12-hour battery life and easy readability.

clarifying_info.q: Has DigiBooks sold products internationally before?
clarifying_info.a: No. DigiBooks has never sold a product outside of the US.

clarifying_info.q: Are there any competitors planning to enter this market?
clarifying_info.a: No competitors in the e-book or tablet space plan to enter this country.

clarifying_info.q: What is the total population of this country?
clarifying_info.a: The total population is 76 million, with a high literacy level.

exhibits.title: Market Segments
exhibits.shows: A table showing three customer segments with their population size and tablet price point for each segment.

exhibits.title: Channel Decisions
exhibits.shows: A table comparing two sales channels (Retail and Internet) across four metrics: reach as a percentage of total potential market, e-book gross margin %, e-reader gross margin %, penetration rate, and overhead costs.

framework: Segmentation, Targeting, and Positioning: Identify which population segments are ideal customers; evaluate size, readership habits, and willingness to pay
Product: Assess whether existing tablet products meet this country's needs or require adaptation; consider e-ink display, battery life, language/content compatibility
Price: Determine appropriate tablet and e-book pricing; consider razor-and-blade model (low tablet price to drive volume, margin on e-books)
Promotion: Identify advertising and marketing mechanisms suited to this market; consider trial-driving tactics given low current usage
Place/Distribution: Evaluate retail vs. internet channel options; consider reach, cost to establish, ability to drive trial, and margin impact
E-book Selection: Assess availability and breadth of e-book catalog relevant to this country's readers

questions.prompt: Using a 3-year projection and Exhibit 1, which segment should DigiBook target? (Note: average e-book price is $10; e-books and tablets carry the same margin; assume all tablet sales happen immediately and ignore time value of money)
questions.guidance: Candidate should calculate 3-year revenue potential for each segment by combining tablet revenue and e-book revenue over 3 years. The segment with the highest total revenue potential should be recommended. Bonus credit for noting that probability of purchase/penetration and TVM are being ignored.

math.setup: Revenue per segment = (Books per year x $10/book x 3 years + Tablet price x 1 tablet) x Segment size
steps: SR Revenue = [(15 books x $10 x 3 years) + $200] x 8M = [$450 + $200] x 8M = $650 x 8M = $5.2B
math.answer: Occasional Readers (OR) has the highest revenue potential at $8.5B and should be the target segment.

questions.prompt: DigiBooks is now considering whether to sell its e-book readers through retail stores or through the internet. How would you evaluate this decision?
questions.guidance: Candidate should weigh pros and cons of each channel. Retail pros: encourages trial of a new product, joint marketing with retailers, retailers can handle customer service and returns. Retail cons: lower margin due to value chain, time and cost to set up, training costs. Internet pros: cheaper to establish, higher margins. Internet cons: hard to encourage trial of an unfamiliar product. Strong answers will connect channel choice back to the market context (low current usage, need to drive trial).

questions.prompt: Based on revised estimates, the e-reader is priced at $100 and the target segment is Occasional Readers (20M people). Using Exhibit 2, estimate the profit potential of the Retail and Internet channels. Which should DigiBooks choose?
questions.guidance: Candidate should use Exhibit 2 data with the given OR segment size (20M) and e-book price ($10) to compute annual profit for each channel net of overhead investment. Key formula: Profit = [(E-books revenue x ebook GM%) + (Tablet revenue x ereader GM%)] x (Segment size x Reach% x Penetration%) - Overheads.

math.setup: Annual Profit = [(10 books x $10/book x ebook GM%) + ($100/tablet x ereader GM%)] x (20M people x Reach% x Penetration%) - Overheads
math.answer: Retail channel yields $300M annual profit vs. Internet at $100M. DigiBooks should choose the Retail channel.

recommendation: DigiBooks should launch its e-book reader targeting the Occasional Reader segment (20M people) through the Retail sales channel.
Based on calculations, the Retail channel is expected to generate $300M in annual profit, compared to $100M via Internet.
risks: Retail channel requires upfront investment ($20M overhead) and time to establish distribution partnerships.
No current e-reader usage (only 1% have used one) means significant consumer education and trial-driving will be needed.
No local manufacturing presence — sourcing from existing US facilities may increase logistics costs or lead times.
If competitors enter the market later, first-mover advantage may erode.
next_steps: Determine advertising mechanisms appropriate for this market to drive awareness and trial.
Decide whether to set up local manufacturing or source from existing US facilities.
Monitor for potential competitor entry into this market.
Evaluate e-book catalog availability and depth for this country's readers.
